newsitem.title: USA: Audi debuts A4 Avant, sees 2,500 sold.
newsitem.headline: Audi debuts A4 Avant, sees 2,500 sold.

text.p: Volkswagen AG unit Audi of America Inc unveiled the newest vehicle in its A4 series, the 1998 A4 Avant Sport Wagon, and said that it expects to sell 2,500 Avants per year.

"We think we will sell conservatively 2,500 per year," vice president in charge of Audi of America Gerd Klauss told a press conference at Avant's North American introduction at the New York International Auto Show.
The car maker also debuted its 1998 A4 2.8 5-valve automobile at the Auto Show Thursday.

Avant was recently launched in Europe, Klauss said. He called the Avant an ideal mix of sport sedan, sport wagon and sport utility vehicle and said the car combines the essential attributes of its 1998 A4 2.8 5-valve sedan with the added convenience and flexibility of a wagon.
Final options and prices have yet to be announced but dealers will begin selling the 1998 Avant in U.S. showrooms this fall.

The Avant features a 30 valve V-6 engine and comes standard with a 5-speed automatic transmission and is available in either front wheel drive or quattro versions. It also features standard front side airbags, in addition to driver and passenger front airbags.

"The A4 Avant is a car that meets consumers' wants and thier needs," Klauss said. "We believe it gives people the driving character they want from a German sport sedan combined with the functionality of a compact-sized wagon - an optimal blend for today's active lifestyles."

Klauss said the 1998 A4 2.8 five-valve takes all the essential attributes of the A4 but offers more power, more control and more choices for the consumer. It is powered by a 2.8-liter double overhead cam V-6 engine with five valves per cylinder. Audi said this combination delivers more power and Klauss said the 1998 A4 2.8 five-valve will be priced in mid-May and the car will go to dealers June 1.
Audi said the five-valve technology adds power and increases combined fuel mileage ratings over the previous two-valve engine.
The car is available in both front wheel drive and quattro versions and comes in standard five-speed manual transmission, although five-speed automatic is available.
Audi sold about 27,400 cars in the U.S. last year, its best year since 1987, Klauss said. He said the company wants to increase U.S. sales volume by 20 percent in 1997.
Klauss said that for the first two months of this year, Audi sold about 4,850 cars in the U.S., an increase of 37 percent over last year.
He said it looks like Audi will sell over 2,500 cars in the U.S. in March. Every Audi model line is strongly ahead of last year in terms of U.S. sales, he said.
The company would like to hit its 20 percent U.S. sales growth projection every year, and wants to reach annual sales volume of 50,000, he said.
"I think (50,000) is a realistic projection," Klauss said.
